values.note: Hawsapple and Spruce primitive sites $18 a night ($126 a week). Plus tax, CPW's reservation fee, and a daily vehicle pass ($10-$15) or an annual state parks pass. The park's electric sites ($36) are at Anthracite Campground, 5 km south.

hookups.source: https://cpw.state.co.us/state-parks/paonia-state-park/paonia-state-park-camping-lodging ('Electrical hook-ups are available only at Anthracite Campground.'; 'water is not available') + cpwshop.com site pages (all 13 Hawsapple/Spruce sites Site Type 'Primitive', no hookup listed), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Hawsapple 7 sites (001-007; 006 is a 35-ft pull-through, 005 30 ft, the rest 10-20 ft) and Spruce 6 sites (008-013, 20-25 ft; 013 a pull-through), ~450 m apart in the canyon at the head of the reservoir. Six people a site. The park's other 7 sites (electric, 50 A) are at Anthracite Campground, ~5 km south on Kebler Pass Road.

values.note: Vault toilets, fire rings and picnic tables; no drinking water in the park, bring your own. No office: the Crawford State Park visitor center serves Paonia.

values.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead. 14 days within a 28-day period. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

note: Two small CPW campgrounds at the head of Paonia Reservoir in a narrow canyon off CO-133, ~16 miles northeast of Paonia below the Ragged Mountains: Spruce, among blue spruce beside the Muddy Creek inflow, and Hawsapple, off County Road 2 toward the boat ramp. --Claude
summary: CPW pages + cpwshop (all 20 site pages): confirmed 13 sites at Hawsapple/Spruce, vault toilets, no drinking water, reservation required on cpwshop. Changed fees 18-36 -> 18 (the $36 electric sites are at Anthracite Campground, 5 km away). Added hookups none (CPW: electric only at Anthracite), max 35 (Hawsapple 006), pull-throughs, season May 1 - Sept 30, fcfs never, 6-month window, 14-in-28 limit. Note trimmed of field facts and the wrong 'up to 7 electric at Hawsapple'.
flags: SPLIT CANDIDATE (separate place): Anthracite Campground, the park's third loop, is ~4.9 km SSW of Hawsapple on County Road 12 (Kebler Pass Road), with its own entrance off that road - beyond the ~1 km rule. cpwshop: 7 sites 017-023, all 'Electric', 'Electricity Hookup: 50', $36/night ($252/week), all Back-In, Maximum Vehicle Length 017 22, 018 25, 019 27, 020 60, 021 60, 022 70, 023 60 (gravel; 018/019 accessible); 020-022 tagged 'Proximity to Water: Riverfront'. Site centroid ~38.94016,-107.35891. On Esri imagery the loop sits on open gravel just south of CR 12; sites 020-022 are ~25-40 m from Anthracite Creek across open ground. Same booking (cpwshop parkID=50034, loop Anthracite), season and no-water rules. Is there already an entry? None named Anthracite in campgrounds.json. Proposed: a new state entry 'Anthracite Campground (Paonia State Park)' at ~38.9402,-107.3590.
The old note said 'up to 7 electric at Hawsapple per CPW' - wrong: CPW says 'Electrical hook-ups are available only at Anthracite Campground'. Removed.

Waterfront re-audit lead (stored riverfront, not changed): the water at Hawsapple/Spruce is the Muddy Creek inflow channel crossing the reservoir's upper sediment flats. On Esri imagery that channel is roughly 10-20 m wide at the sites, which by the size rule is creekside, not riverfront. cpwshop tags Hawsapple 006, 007 and Spruce 008, 009 'Proximity to Water: Lakefront'. Spruce 008/009 look ~15-30 m from the channel in spruce; Hawsapple 005-007 are ~30-60 m from the channel/flats, possibly at the reservoir's high-water edge. Worth a re-audit: creekside vs lakefront (measure to high water) vs riverfront.

Status: CPW 'Paonia State Park Boat Ramp is CLOSED. Hand launched and human powered vessels ... are allowed to launch.' Campgrounds closed for the season (Oct 1 - May 1). No campground closure beyond that.
Pin 38.9838,-107.3459 sits between the loops, ~120 m north of Hawsapple's sites and ~170 m from the 13 Hawsapple/Spruce sites' centroid (38.98516,-107.34678). OK.
Length: Hawsapple 006 (35 ft, pull-through) and 005 (30) are the only sites over 25 ft; Spruce 010-013 take 25 ft. Several Hawsapple sites are 10-20 ft. Fine for a 23-ft rig at 7 sites.
